title: Haiku Observation Output
description: Bounded structured summary returned by Haiku-tier observation (the shift loop's step 2 dispatch and the ci-observer agent). Haiku-tier observers report only API-grounded facts (status codes, build IDs, counts) and closed-taxonomy classifications (anti-pattern IDs, error_class enum). They do NOT quote log content, name files mentioned in logs, or infer line numbers — that work belongs to ci-investigator (Sonnet) which the caller dispatches when specifics are needed. The dispatch_drift field is populated only by ci-observer in validate mode against a predicted pipeline set.

first_failing_stage.description: Name of the first failing Jenkins stage as returned by mcp__jenkins__getBuild — NOT inferred from log content.

primary_failure.description: Categorical classification of the failure — what kind of bucket it falls in. NOT a description of the specific error. Use error_class from the failure-taxonomy.json categories. The source_artifact pointer tells the caller where to dispatch ci-investigator if specifics are needed.

error_class.description: Category from .claude/data/failure-taxonomy.json (e.g. 'DNA_BUILD', 'APP_BUILD', 'INFRASTRUCTURE'). Closed enum — never a free-form description.

source_artifact.description: URL or MCP tool name where the details live. Caller dispatches ci-investigator with this pointer to extract specifics. Examples: 'mcp__jenkins__searchBuildLog jobFullName=elohim-edge/dev buildNumber=42 pattern=error[E', 'https://jenkins.ethosengine.com/job/elohim-genesis/job/dev/966/artifact/genesis/a2o/reports/sprint-report.md'.

observed_anti_patterns.description: Anti-pattern IDs from genesis/agentic/data/anti-patterns.json that matched. Closed taxonomy — Haiku never invents new patterns or describes what they look like; that's already in the catalog.

artifacts_pulled.description: Records of which artifacts ci-observer pulled while observing. Lets the caller dispatch ci-investigator at exactly the right URL without re-discovery. Pure factual record of tool calls — not analysis.

kind.description: What kind of fetch this was.

ref.description: MCP tool call (e.g. 'getBuild jobFullName=elohim-edge/dev buildNumber=42') or full URL.

status.description: Outcome of the fetch. 'empty' = fetched successfully but the artifact had no content (e.g. sprint-report with 0 scenarios).

confidence.description: Confidence that diagnostic-quality data was found, NOT confidence in any analysis. high = artifacts found, status fields all populated, taxonomy match clean. low = artifacts missing, empty, or status unclear (caller should escalate to ci-investigator).

dispatch_drift.description: Populated only by ci-observer in validate mode. Compares the orchestrator's actual pipeline dispatch against a predicted set (typically from graph-walker.mjs run on the diff before push). All fields are factual API responses — predicted comes from the caller, actual comes from the orchestrator's own dispatch list.

verdict.description: expected = predicted == actual; over_built = actual ⊃ predicted; under_built = actual ⊊ predicted; mixed = both extras and missing; recovery_fallback = orchestrator fell into a generic 'build all' or 'baselines stale' mode.

extras.description: Pipelines built that were not predicted.
